newsitem.title: USA: New York judge clears man of Internet date rape.
newsitem.headline: New York judge clears man of Internet date rape.

text.p: A judge on Friday dismissed charges against a New York businessman who was accused of raping a woman he met through the Internet.

Self-employed electronics businessman Paul Krauth, 46, was arrested Sunday for the alleged rape, assault and sodomy of a 41-year-old graduate student from Syracuse, New York, he had contacted online on Feb. 10.
After weeks of exchanging electronic mail, the woman travelled to New York to meet Krauth at his Greenwich Village apartment, police said.
The woman alleged that Krauth raped her there, but prosecutors sought dismissal of the case before Criminal Court Justice Paul Feinman, citing her "lack of candor" to police and attorneys.

Prosecutors said a review of interviews with the woman, the electronic mail with Krauth and a tape recorded message left by the woman on Krauth's telephone answering machine before his arrest showed that "no charges are sustainable against the defendant."

Police and Krauth's lawyer said that on the tape, the woman had left a message for Krauth saying she had "enjoyed the evening" at his apartment, a reaction that ran counter to her allegations of rape and assault.
Krauth's attorney accused the woman of filing a false report. A spokeswoman for the Manhattan District Attorney said no criminal charges would be filed against her.

In November 1996, a Columbia University doctoral candidate, Oliver Jovanovic, was arrested on charges he sexually assaulted a woman he initially met on the Internet. The case is proceeding and Jovanovic is due back in court March 14.
